hook_text: The apple in your lunchbox may have been picked by hand in a valley where it snows in winter.
clip_script: Ceres, in the Western Cape. In winter, snow sits on the mountains and the apple trees are bare. In spring, the orchards turn white with blossom and bees buzz from flower to flower. By late summer, the branches hang heavy with red and green apples. Workers climb ladders and pick each one by hand. In the packhouse the fruit is washed, sorted and packed, then cooled and trucked to the harbour. Some of it will be eaten in faraway countries.
visual_style: Whiteboard orchard drawn through four seasons: bare trees, white blossom, green fruit, red apples, then arrows to a packhouse, a cold store and a ship.
mood: Fresh and bright, like a crisp apple.
pacing: Move through the seasons quickly, then follow one apple from tree to ship.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and look at the sticker on the next apple you eat.
